title: I'm making a CCG in Unity with AI, too early to show progress
author: BuffcatVT
selftext:
I spend a lot of time on it, all my days off about 12 hours a day

I just want people to give the game a try. I know it's gonna use AI art

I know it's gonna use Unity Assets

I can see the negative steam reviews already, Mostly Negative, AI Slop, Asset Flip

I just hope some people find it and enjoy it

Does anyone else get discouraged sometimes?

comments.author: BemaniAK
comments.body: If it's a concern, just commission some art?

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
I don't have the money to commission 1000+ pieces of art 

If I were super rich I'd be all about it, but it's a scale issue and I'm broke

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body: Then why not consider a type of game that is more manageable on the art side?

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
Because I'm passionate about CCGs like MTG and Yugioh

Also their more manageable to code, a good starting place for making a game

replies.author: AxiosXiphos
replies.body: Why not use the tool that provides exactly what the OP needs for next to no cost?

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body: Because it tends to produce subpar results.

replies.author: AxiosXiphos
replies.body: I disagree. I think it can produce incredible results. The issue is entirely the perception about it.

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body: I feel like if you use the first generic prompt with no direction, yeah it's not gonna be great. but with enough time and direction it's more than serviceable

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body:
> but with enough time and direction

Well, *with enough time* you could learn a valuable skill, you know. I would rather spend weeks learning how to get better at Blender for instance, than spending the same amount of time or even less "learning" to get "better" at playing the AI slot machine.

But to each their own.

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
Man I hate blender, I'm more of a unity guy

I can do the basics in blender but I need 2d art assets anyway

It's so easy to lose weeks of work with blender x\_x (skill issue)

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body:
It does tend to converge towards the "AI look".

There have been instances where I saw similar expressions or features (especially about characters) across different games made by different people. If you go to webdev subs you can very quickly spot the kind of website styles it tends to generate.

It is not just perception though. AI has some serious ethical issues (the scraping of materials without consent), which you can overlook if you want, but luckily somebody still cares about that.

replies.author: AxiosXiphos
replies.body: Talking 10's of thousands of dollars and months if not years of work. It's not feasible for single devs

replies.author: BemaniAK
replies.body: No? Who tf are you trying to commission?

replies.author: AxiosXiphos
replies.body: Trading card games are art heavy. For even a starter set you will need upwards of 100 pieces. If every commission costs £50 then you are already looking £5000 before things have really started. And that's making a lot of price assumptions.

replies.author: BemaniAK
replies.body: Do you know what a spritesheet is??

replies.author: Accomplished-Loss9
replies.body: Spritesheets for TCGs? Every card is a unique piece of art. If you have 100 cards you need a 100 unique pieces of art, not a spritesheet.

replies.author: BemaniAK
replies.body: Yeah that's why I asked, because animations are literally 100s of pieces of art, I dunno if you guys know what you're getting into.

comments.author: Big_Presentation2786
comments.body:
No. It's unreasonable to expect an indie dev to spend their own money on commissions.


Especially when the game might not be a success.


If the game sells, and your complaints are mainly because of the art- then maybe look at commissioning some art.


But I don't worry until I know I need to.

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
If the game were successful and made money that would be a whole different story all together 

But it's really not designed to make money from the player base, It's more about letting players build decks, and if they want to support me by buying cards that's an option, but I wouldn't feel comfortable selling packs for more than 50 cents and steam would take like 30% of that

So I wouldn't be making a lot of money

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
You can't say whether or not you are going to make money until you release.


Do your best and be realistic about critic.


I personally don't care about using AI or not. And when I look at what's being created right now, EVERYONE is using AI.


Focus on your gameplay

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
That's what I figured, at least I'm willing to be honest about it

Most companies are using it and not saying anything

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
No one genuinely cares whether or not a game has AI.


The only people I've genuinely experienced bitch and moan about it, is usually the types of people who are moaning because they're bored, insecure with themselves and lonely..


If I worried about people who complained about AI, I'd never get any work done..


If I built a game without AI, they'd still find another reason to complain.

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
Yeah I think it's one of those "you can't satisfy everyone" situations

I just gotta take the path that actually ends in me making the game I want, right?

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
No- you have to forget about everyone else in the world and make the game you always wanted without feeling like 'AI is bad', it's a power tool..


Carpenters use power tools, you're good to follow suit..

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
I agree with the part about AI. But I also think it's important to consider my potential playerbase

But not in any context outside of the game itself

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
If your game is good, they won't care if you use AI.. that's the be all and end all of it..


But it sounds like you know what you're doing 👍

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body: I'll make the game so fun they won't care! that's the plan

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
THIS! This is all you need..


You're ready bro.. you got this!

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body:
Why so unreasonable? That's what we are doing. At least enough to create a prototype that we can pitch to a publisher or failing that, get to an Early Access state.

If you are the first not to believe in your own game...

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
So you're gonna drop a shit ton of money to an artist THEN go see a publisher whose gonna take a shit ton of money to market the game?


It's your call wether or not to drop your own money on a project-
But I don't think you need to -when you look at the rest of the market and how far they are going with AI.


Arc raiders used AI became successful then went back and hired real people to fill in..
That seems more productive and profitable considering you're trying to start a business and it needs to make money first..


I mean how far do you take this?


Drop money on a modeller? Level designer? Sound designer? 


Only then to approach the publisher?
Why struggle when all the power tools exist for you to deliver a product?

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body:
> So you're gonna drop a shit ton of money to an artist THEN go see a publisher whose gonna take a shit ton of money to market the game?

Well yes? I mean it obviously depends on the scale of the game. If you are building another Pong game, then clearly you don't need a publisher (and not even AI). But if you have a vision that would benefit from a larger budget then that seems the only option.

For example, to hire another programmer and cut the development time drastically, we'd need to fork over anywhere between 75-100k€ and for as much as I am investing my own funds in this project, I don't have the risk appetite for that amount.

> when you look at the rest of the market and how far they are going with AI.

Which is? What is the most successful example of a game where a significant part of its art or programming has been generated / vibed? Because all I see are AA/AAA companies using it for placeholders, and then scrambling to remove them once they realise they "forgot" to remove something. What would you say is the Cyberpunk 2077 (or Undertale) of AI developed games?

> Arc raiders used AI became successful then went back and hired real people to fill in.. That seems more productive and profitable considering you're trying to start a business and it needs to make money first..

You could do that of course, but the risks of "souring" the relationship with your potential public are there. Plus, if you have been "in the field" for a bit, you tend to recognise the "AI look" and I don't really want to have that in our game.

> I mean how far do you take this?

> Drop money on a modeller? Level designer? Sound designer? 

Well yes, that's what we have been doing. I am the developer, so I have commissioned art assets that I cannot create (quickly) from people who have demonstrated to have the style I was looking for.

> Only then to approach the publisher? Why struggle when all the power tools exist for you to deliver a product?

I don't think these tools are quite mature yet to get the results I expect. If I look at the type of games posted here on /r/aigamedev, I see a lot of browser games or stuff you could also do with RPGmaker. We are aiming a bit above that level.

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
I'm currently making an RC car video game using AI.. 


I'm literally just using free assets and trying to create the sloppiest game I can under another business name..


Im not spending any money on this thing..


You seem to believe AI is a rarity between gamers and developers.
It's not, it's common as muck.. 


https://aitransparency.scrapeer.com/


My last two games used artists way before AI was prevalent. Everyone hated the art anyway.


If you're afraid of using AI in a game- then your game doesn't have enough gameplay..
It's that simple.


I'm gonna save the art budget this time and buy myself a new car when my new game drops..

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body:
I am aware of that website, but as you can see from the disclosures --- if they are being honest --- among the biggest sellers / most reviewed games, I don't see any that say "all art assets / all code have been generated / vibed."

> If you're afraid of using AI in a game- then your game doesn't have enough gameplay.. It's that simple.

Not even close. I am not "afraid" of AI. I don't like the results it tend to produce.

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
That's ok. 


I love the results it produces..

comments.author: ashareah
comments.body: Proudly sell it as AI art. Society will adapt now or later. Make sure the art looks amazing.

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body: I'll do my best to make it look objectively as good as possible! Thank you

comments.author: LatentBlade
comments.body: I put my game out there early thinking people would hate on AI and I lost perspective on everything other thing that was wrong with it. Look at my post in AI wars to see what I mean. We aren't wrong to worry about haters but we also need to remember other people expect polish too.

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
I'm really hoping that the amount of people who "don't care" about AI art, or care more about polished aesthetics will outweigh the people who will write off the game entirely just because of AI

I mean I'm one person with no budget, if it should be okay for anyone to use it, it's me, right?

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body:
But how literal is it that you are with no budget? AI models cost money too.

Sometimes using AI seems a deliberate choice, because it seems that the money for the subscriptions is there but if it comes to buying even a cheap asset pack, then the money disappears.

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
The budget is whatever pocket money I have left over after paying bills

and it's not a lot, lol

I work an entry level job

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: Just remember no one is going to buy my game or your game because we worked on it alone. We are up against 1000s of other people working hard and get about 10 seconds of someone's attention to show off our game if we're lucky. I'm discouraged but also going to work hard to turn my game around. Best of luck on yours!

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
Yeah I'm definitely not asking for brownie points for being a solo dev

I'm just hoping for grace on the use of AI and unity assets

If they know I'm a solo dev with no budget they might be like "Oh okay it makes sense he had to do it like this"

comments.author: AxiosXiphos
comments.body: Just do it. Advertise clearly that assets were made with a.i. make sure your images avoid the grainy a.i. 'look'; go for a specfic style. If you get review bombed you get review bombed, it's just the cost of using A.I.

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
Yeah I'm hoping if people see "overwhelmingly negative" reviews, and they check and see it's all about the AI, then they will see the game is free, watch the trailer, and try it

Unfortunately a lot of people will see "overwhelmingly negative" and just pass

But it is what it is

comments.author: BellonaSM
comments.body: I am making TCG. Recommed to hire cheap illustraor

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body:
How many illustrations do you need?

How can you tell if the person you're hiring is using AI or not?

replies.author: BellonaSM
replies.body: Good question. I hire student they do not draw from scratch. They only retouching to fix AI error. Hope it help your game

replies.author: BuffcatVT
replies.body: Well that's one way to do it!

replies.author: BellonaSM
replies.body: Even Expefition 33 do the same thing. If you have some main character, it requires some effort.
